what: Royal Caribbean operates cruise ships under the Royal Caribbean, Celebrity and Silversea brands, with a fleet of around 70 ships including partner brands, and it is building private island destinations such as Perfect Day at CocoCay.
customers: Holidaymakers, mainly from North America and Europe, booking cruises directly and through travel agents.
money: drinks packages, excursions, casino, Wi-Fi and private island spending
moat: New ships cost over a billion dollars and take years to build, which caps how fast capacity can grow, and its private destinations cannot be copied by rivals.
risks: Debt of about $23 billion remains from the pandemic shutdown
Fuel prices and currency moves affect costs directly
Any health scare, accident or geopolitical event stops bookings quickly
Cruising is discretionary spending that falls early in a recession
opportunities: Pricing has stayed strong and onboard spending per passenger keeps rising
Private destinations raise margins because the spending stays within the company
New larger ships lower the cost per passenger berth
watch: Net yields, which combine occupancy and pricing, and the pace of debt reduction.
